meta.note: Single source of truth for the funding record. /projects/ is generated from this file by tools/build_projects.py; tools/export_projects_docx.py produces the table for application documents. Amounts are the awarded volumes for the subprojects applied for and managed personally, in thousand euro.

roles.subproject: Subproject lead — own subproject applied for and managed

meta.funding_lines_note: Number of distinct funding programmes, maintained by hand — it cannot be derived from the funder column, since several projects share one line.
meta.ongoing_note: 'Ongoing' is derived from the end date, never stored — a project counts as running while (to, to_month) >= (current year, current month). to_month is optional and defaults to 12; give it whenever a project ends mid-year, otherwise the site keeps showing it as active until January. That way the website cannot claim a finished project is still running.
meta.lab_pages: Eighteen of these have a fuller description on the lab site. The URL is built from the project id, because the two sites agree on it; lab_id records the handful where they do not, and "lab": true marks the ones where they do. Six projects have no lab page — small industry contracts and the post-doctoral fellowship — and simply carry no link. Writing a second description here instead would guarantee the two drift apart, which is the failure this repository keeps finding.
meta.detail_blocks: Every project has a detail block, generated from tags/desc/links here. They used to be hand-written HTML for twelve of the twenty-four, which is why the other twelve had none.

without_own_volume.name: Bernstein Focus Neurotechnology — Berlin
without_own_volume.blurb: Neurotechnologies for intuitive and efficient human–machine interaction.
desc: Neurotechnologies for improving intuitive and efficient human–machine interaction. The Bernstein Focus: Neurotechnology Berlin brought together a multidisciplinary faculty to apply insights from basic neuroscience directly to real-world applications, with a focus on non-invasive „brain reading" techniques.

Within it, project A3 „Neuro-Usability": Neurotechnologies for Human-Machine Interaction used biosignal sensors to measure and model aspects of usability — efficiency, satisfaction and joy of use. This is where my psychophysiological measurement approach originates.
